feed.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
feed.subtitle: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

entry.title: Ms. Rachel has entered her album era, and she is so happy about it
entry.summary: Ms. Rachel has conquered YouTube, Netflix and the toy aisle. Now she's making an album, with real instruments, big feelings and her littlest listeners in mind.

entry.title: Judge rules court must get notice as Trump threatens to tear down Kennedy Center
entry.summary: A judge told President Trump Thursday that he can't tear down The Kennedy Center –- at least not without 30 days' notice.

entry.title: Attorney fighting Trump's efforts to rename and close Kennedy Center discusses case
entry.summary: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with Norm Eisen, whose legal group Democracy Defenders Action has been fighting the Trump administration in court over its efforts to rename and close the Kennedy Center.

entry.title: White House withdraws nomination of Lance Schroyer to lead ICE
entry.summary: President Trump's nominee to lead U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement was former Oklahoma state trooper Lance Schroyer. Three months after tapping him for the job, his name is being withdrawn.

entry.title: Republican 'cavalry' arrives with a Trump-backed $150 million ad blitz in key races
entry.summary: To counter a difficult political environment, two Trump-aligned super PACs have reserved more than $150 million in ads — primarily in deep red House and Senate races that have now become competitive.

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: Trump threatens to tear down the Kennedy Center amid court battle, Trump's other priorities also get pushback this week, Poland's PM warns Russia could strike countries that support Ukraine.

entry.title: Some GOP candidates are still making election fraud claims. Voters want to move on
entry.summary: President Trump and some Republican battleground candidates are still embracing false claims about widespread election fraud in 2020, even as many GOP voters want them to move on.

entry.title: Republican candidate in Florida runs ads criticizing Trump's immigration enforcement
entry.summary: In a rare move, a House Republican running in a competitive race in South Florida is publicly breaking with President Trump. Maria Elvira Salazar represents a majority Hispanic district.

entry.title: Stocks hit records as AI optimism grows, but bond markets tell a different story
entry.summary: The stock market is at record highs, largely thanks to tech stocks that are benefitting from investor optimism about the AI boom. But bond markets may be telling a different story.

entry.title: Texas Republican candidate under fire for comment about university students of color
entry.summary: A Texas Republican's complaint that too many people of color were in a video of the crowd at a University of Texas football game set off condemnations.
